newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares steady, light profit taking seen.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares steady, light profit taking seen.

text.p: Singapore shares were steady at the open on Wednesday with profit taking seen after the surge in prices late Tuesday.
"Prices are off their highs though they are still up. The profit taking has been well absorbed so far this morning," said a broker with a local firm.
Dealers said sentiment remained firm with Wall Street gaining for the third consecutive session and calm returning to the Malaysian market after last week's sell off.

After about an hour of trading, the Straits Times Industrial index was up 4.67 points toi 2,109.38. The UOB-OTC index for Malaysian issues traded over the counter was up 6.99 points to 1,233.36. Market volume was 57 million units with 186 gainers overwhelming 31 losers.

Among the actives was newly listed electronics distributor Serial System with over three million shares traded. It was at S$0.61, against its offer price of S$0.58. Malaysia's Berjaya Industrial topped the actives list with 8.4 million shares traded including a block of 6.5 million crossed at S$1.84.
Van Der Horst shares rose 18 cents to S$4.94 on reports that the value of its investments had risen sharply. SIA foreign gained 20 cents to S$12.00.
